title: AI agents exploit medical software flaw to access university server
summary:
Amazon said attackers used autonomous AI agents to find and exploit a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, open-source medical-imaging software, during a September campaign against universities in East Asia. The agents went from mapping the software’s interface to writing files on a server in about 11 minutes; in a later session, they used the flaw to obtain root access. Amazon linked the activity with moderate confidence to a China-linked actor, but did not identify a group or establish government involvement [thehackernews.com#1][securityweek.com#1].

Separately, a wave of U.S. outages from Nov. 12 to 17 affected Microsoft services, banking, Apple apps, aviation and an NSA network. Officials cited technical failures and patching problems, not evidence of a coordinated cyberattack; some vulnerabilities behind the repairs had been found with AI [wired.com#1][theguardian.com#1][pbs.org#1].

MONAI Label maintainers merged a source-code fix on Oct. 19 but had not yet issued a patched release [thehackernews.com#1].
quote: The patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild. So that’s going to create its instability.
quote_author: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella
talking_points: Separate cyberattack: Criminals compromised the legitimate marketing platform Optimizely and planted malicious code on more than 170 websites, including the BBC, CNN and Zoom, to steal payment details and redirect about US$7,000 [scroll.in#1].

Policy review: A U.S. Government Accountability Office assessment published Nov. 20 set out 16 policy options, including standardized testing and stronger safeguards for AI model lifecycles [casrai.org#1].

Exploit gap: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency listed 300 vulnerabilities as exploited in 2026, while VulnCheck counted 1,500. Both figures are far below the more than 100,000 vulnerabilities found overall [wired.com#1].

VPN exposure: TeamT5 chief executive Tsai Song-ting said attacks on web servers and VPN devices have increased and warned that a compromised VPN can give attackers direct access to a company’s internal network [cna.com.tw#1].

Cybersecurity hiring: Microsoft issued more than 1,400 product security patches in October—about 10 times its historic baseline—while US cybersecurity hiring has lagged overall hiring, according to LinkedIn data reviewed by The New York Times [nzherald.co.nz#2].

Open-source burden: A significant share of internet infrastructure relies on open-source software maintained by small volunteer teams, leaving some widely used components with limited resources for security fixes [nzherald.co.nz#1][bridgewater.com#1].
Patch volume: The number of software vulnerabilities recorded in 2026 passed 100,000, compared with about 25,000 in 2022, according to Wired [wired.com#1].

Patch race: Bridgewater said the average time from vulnerability disclosure to exploitation fell from about a month to 11 days, while the number of recorded flaws under active exploitation surged [bridgewater.com#1].

Prompt exposure: Dragos said a five-month test using nearly two million canary-laced prompts found evidence of data exposure at three AI providers and prompt access by inference-marketplace resellers [dragos.com#1].

Hidden flaw: Cybersecurity researcher Paulos Yibelo used AI tools to find a Ghostscript flaw that allowed an uploaded file with a specially crafted font to trigger malicious code. The software developer and affected companies issued fixes after he notified them [kathimerini.gr#1].

perspectives.text: Former U.S. cybersecurity agency director Chris Krebs: Microsoft, IBM and Google are using frontier AI models to find bugs before attackers do, Krebs said. He argued that defenders should keep using AI to identify and patch those bugs [pbs.org#1].

TeamT5 cybersecurity: Chief executive Tsai Song-ting argued that companies cannot rely on fully automated AI defense because defenders bear the consequences of mistaken decisions. He recommended prioritizing critical assets and temporarily taking a system offline when a severe flaw cannot be fixed quickly [cna.com.tw#1].

OpenRouter: The AI router said it had removed three providers and revoked Zero Data Retention eligibility for 125 endpoints after Dragos’s findings. It said the research did not show a breach of OpenRouter itself [rescana.com#1].

Satya Nadella, Microsoft chief executive: Nadella warned that much critical infrastructure runs firmware that cannot be patched, citing chillers, heating and cooling systems, and internet-connected transport networks [thenextweb.com#1].

Christopher Krebs, former director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency: Krebs warned that AI-enabled offensive frameworks are scanning company networks continuously for vulnerabilities, eroding the time defenders once had to respond [pbs.org#1].

Mahmoud Elkhodr, senior lecturer in information and communication technologies at CQUniversity Australia: Elkhodr calls for governments to require critical-service operators to test how long they can keep core functions running without their usual global technology providers [scroll.in#1].

technical_details: Root access chain: In a later session, agents planted a Python startup file and triggered a training process that loaded it, creating a reverse shell with the privileges of the server account [thehackernews.com#1][securityaffairs.com#1].

Microsoft gateway failures: A gateway-server patch deployed in July contained a latent defect. A shift of Teams traffic to a shared gateway coincided with reduced system capacity, and automated traffic rerouting added load as servers failed [kienthuc.net.vn#1].

Disclosure-to-exploitation window: Bridgewater’s analysis says the average time from vulnerability disclosure to exploitation has fallen from about a month to 11 days, increasing the risk that attackers exploit a flaw before downstream users install its patch [bridgewater.com#1].

AI inference routing: An inference router may forward prompts through several providers, each able to see the full request and response; Dragos said privacy settings such as Zero Data Retention were not consistently honored across the chain [dragos.com#1].

MONAI Label path traversal: The vulnerable upload function appended a user-supplied file identifier to a storage path without checking that the resolved file remained inside the approved folder; the default server configuration also lacked authentication [thehackernews.com#1].
industry_impact: Medical-imaging research: MONAI Label is a server used by research teams to annotate medical scans and train imaging models; it is separate from the broader MONAI framework [thehackernews.com#1].
Service disruption fallout: The Microsoft outage halted routine procedures such as releasing detainees from US jails and accessing some patient records at UK hospitals [theguardian.com#1].

AI service providers: Dragos said stolen canary credentials were used in attempts to access its controlled test systems and AWS accounts, showing how exposed prompt data can put connected cloud resources at risk [dragos.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: What signs should operators check for if a MONAI Label server was reachable?
suggested_qna.answer: Administrators should look for unexpected Python startup files and unusual training jobs, which could indicate the file-write flaw was used to launch code [thehackernews.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: Did Amazon confirm a second university was compromised?
suggested_qna.answer: No. Amazon said agents later received a tunnel into a second university network running the same software, but it had not confirmed that network was compromised [thehackernews.com#1].

user_action_items: Restrict exposed MONAI Label servers: Block untrusted network access, enable authentication, run the service with a limited account and verify that any source build includes the fix before treating it as patched [thehackernews.com#1].

Review AI-provider prompt handling: Check router and provider incident notices, rotate credentials previously included in prompts, and ask vendors where prompts are routed and retained [rescana.com#1].
historical_background: In 1991, a typo in new code from telephone company DSC Communications helped take down millions of phone lines over several months. The company had skipped its customary 13-week testing period because it considered the upgrades minor [nzherald.co.nz#1].

title: Anthropic AI proof clears formal checks, but human review remains
summary:
An AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis by Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge has passed formal checks by two groups: the Lean Focused Research Organization, which advances the Lean proof system, and the Mathlib Initiative, which supports its mathematics library. The groups said on Nov. 21 they had “full confidence” in the proof Alpöge developed with Anthropic’s Claude model [theguardian.com#1][nacionale.com#1][unite.ai#1].

The checks establish that the formalized code proves the Riemann hypothesis as defined in Mathlib, but do not provide mathematicians with a readable account of the argument. The proof consists of a Lean library of about 17 million lines, and Alpöge has said the argument is too large to present as a conventional paper at this stage [unite.ai#1][indiatoday.in#1][dw.com#1].

The certification does not constitute formal acceptance of the problem as solved. The Clay Mathematics Institute requires a solution to appear in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand at least two years of scrutiny before it can consider awarding its $1 million prize [thejournal.ie#1][nacionale.com#1].
quote: I imagine the digestion process will take some time, though in this case at least we have a human author to communicate with to assist with this task.
quote_author: Terence Tao, mathematician
talking_points: Human alternative: Stanford professor Ravi Vakil said postdoctoral researcher Alessandro Masullo had submitted an independent, AI-free draft concerning the generalized Riemann hypothesis; the manuscript still needs substantial revision and review [heise.de#1][inside.com.tw#1].

Broader claim: Alpöge said his method also extends to the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; that claim is separate from the certification of the Riemann-hypothesis proof [dallasexpress.com#1][thedefiant.io#1].
Prize conditions: The Clay Mathematics Institute selected the hypothesis as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems and offers $1 million for an accepted solution [thejournal.ie#1][thehindu.com#1].

Audit results: MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland reported that all 175,187 Lean modules compiled without errors; an axiom audit found that the five headline theorems relied only on Lean’s three standard axioms [nacionale.com#1][unite.ai#1].

Independent checkers: Lean’s kernel and third-party checkers accepted the formal proof export, while the tools comparator and con-leche separately confirmed that the encoded theorem matches Mathlib’s Riemann-hypothesis statement [unite.ai#1][indiatoday.in#1].
Historical reach: Efforts to prove the hypothesis helped develop techniques used in algebraic geometry, probability theory, quantum physics and dynamical systems [thehindu.com#1].

Model access: Alpöge said he worked with a non-public version of Claude for about six weeks, limiting outside researchers’ ability to reproduce the discovery process with the same model [bbc.com#1][theguardian.com#1].
Parallel claim: Stanford professor Ravi Vakil said a postdoctoral researcher in his department had independently submitted a proof of the hypothesis [thejournal.ie#1].
Broader claim: Alpöge also said the approach proves the generalized Riemann hypothesis, which extends the conjecture to related L-functions [thehindu.com#1][thejournal.ie#1][heise.de#1].

perspectives.text: Ngô Bảo Châu, Fields Medal-winning mathematician: He argued that fears that mathematical research is ending are misplaced, and described AI as a tool that could expand mathematical work and make it more accessible [36kr.com#1].

James Maynard, Oxford number theorist: He said he suspects the proof will be correct, while cautioning that checking it will take time and understanding why it works will require substantial effort [nacionale.com#3].

Andrew Sutherland, MIT mathematician: He said he was both nervous and excited about the future, noting that researchers may need years to understand how the proof works and where its methods can be applied [thehindubusinessline.com#1].

Brian Conrey, a leading specialist on the Riemann hypothesis, said he had not yet seen a manuscript and had asked for a copy. He also thought there might be simpler ways to present the proof [thejournal.ie#1].

title: Anthropic IPO tests AI safety promises against public-market pressure
summary:
Anthropic, the maker of Claude and described as the first pure AI lab to go public, began trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. Its shares fell the next day during a wider technology selloff as the company faces pressure to fund costly computing needs and sustain growth [theverge.com#1][lavanguardia.com#1][wsj.com#2].

Critics cited by NPR say demands for shareholder returns could weigh on decisions such as delaying a risky model for additional safety testing. Anthropic’s prospectus warns that safeguards may prove inadequate or be circumvented, and says the company could ultimately lose control of its models [npr.org#1]. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has said safety and public benefit are built into the company’s mission [npr.org#1].

Anthropic has made large, long-term infrastructure commitments and uses chips from Nvidia, AMD, Google and Amazon for model training and inference, according to reporting on its filings and supplier relationships [tmtpost.com#1][lemonde.fr#1]. Its Long-Term Benefit Trust can appoint four of seven directors, and the company markets its safety approach to enterprise and government customers [npr.org#1][wersm.com#1].
quote: “There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety.”
quote_author: Dario Amodei, Anthropic chief executive
talking_points: Supplier investment: Seven semiconductor and technology suppliers bought non-voting shares in Anthropic’s private placement, giving them a financial stake in a major customer [tmtpost.com#1].
Share supply: About 300 million additional Anthropic shares are due to become tradable on Dec. 15, which some investors said could add pressure to the stock [faz.net#1].
Customer stakes: Anthropic markets its safety approach to enterprise and government customers concerned with security, data handling and predictable model behavior [wersm.com#1].
Safety governance: Anthropic is a public benefit corporation; its Long-Term Benefit Trust can appoint four of seven directors, while the founders control appointments to the other three [npr.org#1].

Trust dissolution: Legal experts cited by NPR said the founders and shareholders with voting rights could dissolve the trust, potentially allowing them to override its influence during a major safety dispute [npr.org#1].

Enterprise demand: Anthropic reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in revenue over the preceding 12 months as of September, compared with about 1,500 in 2025; its revenue run rate reached $81 billion by Oct. 31 [businesstimes.com.sg#1].
Index buying: Intropic estimates funds tracking stock indexes could buy as much as 30% of Anthropic’s shares by year-end, though those purchases are not guaranteed [indiatimes.com#1].
Bank fees: The deal generated $550 million in fees for Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and 20 other banks, according to Bloomberg data cited by The Business Times [businesstimes.com.sg#1].
Options trading: Options on Anthropic shares were expected to start trading the following week, giving investors another way to bet on or hedge against price swings [indiatimes.com#1].

perspectives.text: Jonathan Golub, chief equity strategist at Seaport Research Partners, said the AI-stock selloff looked excessive and demand for computing power remained strong. He identified financing hundreds of billions of dollars in new infrastructure as a challenge [bloomberg.com#4].

Avery Marquez, Renaissance Capital investment-strategy director: Marquez said the valuation debate and uncertainty about an AI bubble have become more pronounced because Anthropic is a newly listed stock, and that investors need time for price discovery [cnbc.com#1].

Jonathan Golub, Seaport Research Partners chief equity strategist: Golub argued that the AI-driven market selloff looked excessive because demand for computing power remained strong and semiconductor earnings expectations were rising, while warning that markets must still finance hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure [bloomberg.com#1].

title: Developers publish manifesto urging human review of AI-generated work
summary:
Software developers and attendees at the AIE Code Summit published a “No AI Slop” manifesto on Nov. 22, urging people to take responsibility for AI-assisted work and review outputs according to the stakes. The signatories warn that AI agents can produce more code and documentation than a person can assess, while unchecked errors can be copied into later work [github.com#1].

A study of local open-weight models found that agents often identified the vulnerable code and formed a correct hypothesis but failed to produce a working input that would trigger the vulnerability [arxiv.org#1]. Separately, Together AI said an AI coding agent committed a repository credential that enabled an unauthorized party to download stored prompt samples. The company said it was continuing to review potentially exposed customer data [together.ai#1].
quote: AI cannot replace human judgement, it can only amplify our judgement (or lack thereof).
quote_author: AIE Code Summit 2026 speakers and attendees
talking_points: Trace failures: A case study of 100 support-agent traces recorded 12 failures, including seven cases in which the agent asked for details instead of calling a tool and two involving misapplied policy rules [github.com#2].

Security changes: Together AI said it made zero data retention the default for new accounts, added credential checks to pull requests and changed development rules for AI coding agents [together.ai#1].

Model testing: Researchers tested 12 local model configurations on 10 vulnerability-reproduction tasks. Every configuration handled most of the six easier tasks, while the four harder tasks required the 27-billion-parameter model [arxiv.org#1].

Review standard: The manifesto argues that success should be measured by what users receive and how it helps them, rather than code volume, merged pull requests or the number of agents running [github.com#1].

perspectives.text: Together AI: The company said it is investigating what customer information may have been exposed and will notify affected customers directly; it advised customers handling sensitive prompts to enable zero data retention [together.ai#1].

title: FBI probes crime-database breach as hackers target USDA payment system
summary:
The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a database used by federal, state and local law enforcement, while the U.S. Department of Agriculture separately told employees that hackers targeted a system used to pay farmers [securityweek.com#1][channel3000.com#1][dawn.com#1]. Officials have not established whether the incidents are connected or who was responsible [dawn.com#1][engadget.com#1].

The scope of the FBI incident remains unclear: it is not known whether attackers accessed sensitive NCIC records or stole information. The FBI has not publicly confirmed the incident or responded to requests for comment [bleepingcomputer.com#1][securityweek.com#1]. A former FBI official warned that inaccurate NCIC records could affect officers’ decisions and public safety [channel3000.com#1]. Former USDA officials told NBC News that access to the payment system could provide a route to more sensitive food-safety data and research on animal-borne illnesses [dawn.com#1][pcmag.com#1].

President Donald Trump called the reported FBI breach “not good,” then suggested it might reveal information about voter fraud [securityweek.com#1][theverge.com#1]. ABC News reported that NCIC would not hold information on the Russia and Ukraine investigations Trump also invoked [abc7chicago.com#1]. The FBI and USDA incidents are being described as cyberattacks, distinct from recent service outages that officials attributed to routine system upgrades and vulnerability fixes [dawn.com#1][securityweek.com#1].
quote: Officers need to know that when they run somebody through NCIC, the information coming back is accurate.
quote_author: Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack
talking_points: ShinyHunters arrests: The FBI investigation into the September jobs-portal breach led to arrests of suspected members of the ShinyHunters group, including a Canadian cybersecurity executive reportedly linked to the attacks [bleepingcomputer.com#1].

Disrupted services: A nationwide aviation halt disrupted more than 18,000 flights, while a global Microsoft outage affected hundreds of millions of users. Officials said the outages were not evidence of cyberattacks [business-standard.com#1][dawn.com#1][securityweek.com#1].

Cyber director: The White House fired National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross during the week of the reported breaches, as criticism mounted over outages affecting key services [dawn.com#1][capitalfm.africa#1].

perspectives.text: Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack: Pack said NCIC’s nationwide links are important to understanding how an attacker might have entered the system [abc7chicago.com#1].

FBI Director Kash Patel: Patel said the bureau was strengthening defenses through Operation Winter Shield and said the administration was making overdue updates to key systems [channel3000.com#1][thisday.com.ng#1].

title: GTA 6 launches at 30 fps as leak fuels unofficial PC port efforts
summary:
Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, targeting 30 frames per second on every console to preserve the density of its environments and crowds. Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said the PlayStation 5 Pro’s stronger graphics processor improves effects such as ray-traced shadows, but its CPU cannot handle the game’s complex simulation at 60 fps [mmorpg.com#1]. Rockstar has not announced a PC release date [cnnturk.com#1].

An Xbox Quick Resume glitch can remove the frame-rate cap on Series X. Players report 45 to 100 fps, but the glitch also speeds up gameplay and causes inconsistent performance in crowded areas [neowin.net#1][wccftech.com#1]. Reports on Series S performance conflict: Digital Foundry testing cited by IOL found frame rates in the low 20s during heavy explosions, while early hands-on reviews described smooth play [iol.co.za#1][mashable.com#1]. Some PS5 players also report crashes that block story progress; Rockstar has not confirmed a fix [eurogamer.net#1].

An anonymous leaker known as Cyberleek says a 209 GB Xbox build is available but has withheld the executable, promising to release it Nov. 23. The files have not been independently confirmed as genuine [decrypt.co#1]. A separate volunteer project, Leonida, says its recompilation work cannot yet boot the game and its developers need the executable to begin that step [github.com#1].
quote: This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps.
quote_author: Cyberleek
talking_points: Player engagement: On launch day, 61% of active U.S. PlayStation 5 users and 56% of global Xbox users played GTA VI. Players averaged 513 minutes on PlayStation and 494 on Xbox, Circana adviser Mat Piscatella said [thegamer.com#1].

Console network: PlayStation Network experienced scattered outages before launch but recovered quickly, and preload downloads had no widespread failures. The eventual launch of GTA Online will pose a larger network test, Push Square said [pushsquare.com#1].
Crash reports: Some Xbox Series X players also reported crashes, and Rockstar support directed players with console error codes to Sony or Microsoft for help [eurogamer.net#1].

Crypto condition: Decrypt reported that Cyberleek offered to release the executable early if its CYBERLEEK token reached a market value of $15 million. The token’s market value was around $1.3 million at the time [decrypt.co#1].
PC groundwork: Leonida says it has translated 26,503 Xbox graphics shaders into SPIR-V, but its graphics layer still lacks pipelines, draw calls and a swapchain [github.com#1].

perspectives.text: Xbox Series S players: Mashable’s reviewer urged players who cannot upgrade not to let console comparisons spoil the experience, arguing the game remains immersive on Series S despite unknown graphical trade-offs [mashable.com#1].
Leonida developers: The project says it is built from users’ own readable game files and does not decrypt them or bypass protection [github.com#1].

title: Rockstar says GTA VI generated record $3.79 billion on launch day
summary:
Rockstar Games said Grand Theft Auto VI generated an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, Nov. 19, calling it the biggest entertainment launch in history. The new entry in the crime-game series sold 32.5 million copies before release and is available only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S [channel3000.com#1][theguardian.com#1][digitaltrends.com#1].

The $3.79 billion represents estimated customer spending at retail, not the amount Rockstar or parent company Take-Two Interactive received after retailers and platform operators took their shares [technews.city#1]. The figure is nearly five times the roughly $800 million estimated for predecessor Grand Theft Auto V’s first 24 hours in 2013; GTA V later sold nearly 235 million copies [foxbusiness.com#1][bluewin.ch#1].

Neither a PC edition nor the online multiplayer component has a confirmed release date. Analysts at Wells Fargo forecast sales of 65 million copies by Take-Two’s fiscal year-end in March 2027, while TD Cowen analyst Doug Creutz said the scale and timing of future recurring spending in GTA Online matter more to the company’s stock than unit sales alone [bluewin.ch#1][indianexpress.com#1].
quote: We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you
quote_author: Sam Houser, president and founder of Rockstar Games
talking_points: Review divide: Metacritic showed a 99/100 average from about 150 professional reviews but a 5.5/10 user score from nearly 45,000 ratings, with some players criticizing bugs, originality and the lack of a 60-frame-per-second mode [bluewin.ch#1].
Player engagement: Circana data cited by TechSpot found 61% of active U.S. PlayStation 5 owners and 56% of active Xbox owners worldwide played the game on launch day [techspot.com#1].
Audience beyond consoles: Stream Charts counted more than 132 million hours of GTA VI viewing across Twitch, YouTube and Kick on launch day [technews.city#1].

Launch-day absences also rose: BrightHR reported a 56% increase in UK sickness absence versus the previous Thursday, while provisional data suggested about 35,000 more secondary school pupils missed school [techspot.com#1].

perspectives.text: Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick: Earlier this month, Zelnick said the company was not ready to declare success before the launch because it avoids claiming success before it occurs [indianexpress.com#1].

U.S. police departments: Several departments warned players not to imitate the game’s car thefts, reckless driving and violence; Atlanta police wrote, “GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!” [theguardian.com#1].

title: Signal details mobile screen-capture controls, including timed opt-outs
summary:
Signal has detailed mobile controls designed to stop operating-system AI agents from reading chats displayed in its encrypted messaging app. The protections are available on iPhones running iOS 27 or later with Signal 8.37 or later, and on Android with Signal 8.35.1 or later [finchannel.com#1]. They address the risk that agents can inspect a conversation after it has been decrypted for display, beyond Signal’s control [computerbase.de#1][techcrunch.com#1].

On iPhone, users can turn off the protection or pause it for 10 minutes; on Android, Signal activates Screen security when it detects an assistant trying to read the screen [finchannel.com#1][apfeltalk.de#1]. Signal says these screen-capture measures do not block other routes to on-device data, and it cannot reliably provide the same protection on macOS [thehackernews.com#1][finchannel.com#1].
quote: In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that's on your screen.
quote_author: Meredith Whittaker, president of the Signal Foundation
talking_points: Developer requests: Signal wants Apple, Google and Microsoft to offer a documented opt-out covering screen reading, file access, notifications, APIs and other operating-system pathways [thehackernews.com#1][coywolf.com#1].

Agent permissions: Meta’s Muse agent accessed Signal on Android through notification permissions and on a Mac through accessibility and screenshot tools, according to reported examples [thehackernews.com#1][indiatimes.com#1].

Android override: Signal says it will restore protection after 90 days if an Android user disables it through a Screen security prompt; disabling it directly in Privacy settings does not trigger reminders [finchannel.com#1].

perspectives.text: Signal: The company said it is discussing with Apple and Google how to make their systems work better with privacy-sensitive apps [coywolf.com#1].
Meta: Meta said agents need to see and interact with users’ computers to act on their behalf, and that Muse accesses other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant [indiatimes.com#1].

title: Mexico captures FBI-wanted cartel leader in raid that leaves 11 dead
summary:
Mexican forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday night, Nov. 20, in an operation that left four soldiers and seven suspected cartel gunmen dead, Mexico’s Defense Ministry said. Meza Flores, who was flown to Mexico City, is on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list. U.S. authorities accuse him of trafficking drugs and illegally possessing firearms [pbs.org#1][theguardian.com#1][nytimes.com#1].

The raid triggered armed clashes, vehicle burnings and roadblocks across parts of Sinaloa. Videos showed baseball fans fleeing gunfire in Guasave, while local authorities urged residents to stay indoors. The government said U.S. intelligence helped locate Meza Flores; The New York Times reported that U.S. and Mexican authorities had shared intelligence for weeks [npr.org#1][krdo.com#1][nytimes.com#3].

Meza Flores was allied with Los Mayos, a faction fighting for control of the Sinaloa Cartel after its co-founder Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada was taken into U.S. custody in 2024. President Donald Trump has pressed Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to intensify action against cartels, including by linking trade policy to security progress. Meza Flores is now in the custody of Mexican prosecutors, and the United States has sought his extradition [koreatimes.co.kr#1][ft.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].
quote: We’re working with her on the cartels because the cartels are running Mexico. I told her that. And we can’t let the cartels run Mexico. They’re our neighbour
quote_author: President Donald Trump
talking_points: Other detainees: Authorities said eight people were arrested overall: Meza Flores and two senior associates were taken to Mexico City, while five others remained in Sinaloa [theguardian.com#1][cbsnews.com#1].
Weapons seized: Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities recovered a.50-caliber rifle, a grenade launcher and hand grenades, as well as drugs and cash [aaj.tv#1][cbsnews.com#1].
Baseball suspended: The Mexican Pacific League canceled the remaining weekend games after gunfire disrupted the Guasave match [krdo.com#1][mediafax.ro#1].
Reward offer: The U.S. State Department had offered up to $5 million for information leading to Meza Flores’ arrest [dw.com#1][theguardian.com#1].

Additional allegations: When the FBI added Meza Flores to its most-wanted list in 2025, it also cited alleged kidnapping, extortion and torture; these remain allegations [bbc.co.uk#1][indianexpress.com#1].

perspectives.text: Mexican Security Minister Omar García Harfuch: He called the arrests an important step toward pacifying Sinaloa and said federal security forces would remain deployed to protect residents [lavanguardia.com#1][nigerianeye.com#1].

Security experts: Experts cited by the Financial Times questioned whether removing cartel leaders can curb violence without stronger policing and efforts to address political corruption and money laundering [ft.com#1].

title: COP31 final draft omits fossil fuels, leaving deal at risk
summary:
COP31 negotiators in Antalya were still seeking consensus on Sunday after a proposed final agreement again omitted an explicit commitment to move away from fossil fuels, the central dispute at the U.N. climate summit [al-monitor.com#1][bbc.com#2][thehindu.com#1]. The draft refers indirectly to a 2023 agreement on the transition, recognizes that the world is on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius warming threshold, and backs a goal of raising electricity’s share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035. It also calls for faster development of carbon-removal technologies [al-monitor.com#1][abc.net.au#1].

The text followed overnight consultations among summit co-presidents Turkey and Australia and delegations from nearly 200 countries. It does not restore the proposed $120 billion annual adaptation-finance target that developing countries had sought, and it sets no requirement that new power for the electricity goal come from renewables [premiumtimesng.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

Countries still needed to approve the proposed text. The scheduled session was delayed, and reports did not confirm that a final agreement had been adopted [bbc.co.uk#1][thehindu.com#1]. Departing delegations could also reduce attendance below the two-thirds quorum needed for a decision [ft.com#1].
quote: It’s better to have no deal than to have a bad deal.
quote_author: Wopke Hoekstra, European Union climate commissioner
talking_points: Carbon capture dispute: The latest text scaled back its commitments to carbon capture, use and storage, which may be enough to ease the EU’s concerns [bbc.co.uk#2].

Finance dispute: The latest draft replaces the $120 billion target with further discussions on a pathway to triple adaptation finance, while leaving countries’ contributions voluntary [premiumtimesng.com#1].

Electricity claims: A document sent anonymously to some delegations from poorer countries portrayed the proposed electrification goal as binding national quotas, although the UN described it as a global target, with countries free to choose their own pathways [dw.com#1].
Import savings: The International Energy Agency estimated that electrification could save developing countries about $100 billion in fossil-fuel imports by 2035 [dw.com#1].
Roadmap gap: The draft also omits a Brazil-led global roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels, a demand of several countries and campaign groups [premiumtimesng.com#1].
Global stocktake: The 2028 global stocktake is intended to assess countries’ climate efforts and shape subsequent emissions-cutting plans [dw.com#1].

Carbon capture: The draft retains an aspirational aim to scale carbon capture, use and storage toward one gigatonne by 2035, despite opposition from delegates and campaigners [premiumtimesng.com#1][thehindu.com#1].

Science timetable: Countries also disagree over when the next Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change assessment reports should appear: several want them before the 2028 global stocktake, while India and Saudi Arabia favor 2029 [straitstimes.com#1][index.hr#1].

perspectives.text: COP31 President Murat Kurum, Turkey’s environment minister, said he believed the new text could win agreement and urged delegates to weigh it carefully, saying people outside the negotiating hall were already experiencing climate impacts [abc.net.au#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

title: France protests enter sixth weekend as turnout falls and clashes flare
summary:
Protesters in France demonstrated over living costs and public services for a sixth consecutive Saturday on Nov. 21, with the Interior Ministry counting 82,500 participants nationwide and organizers estimating 150,000. Both figures were down from the previous weekend and far below the 800,000 organizers said had joined the first large march on Oct. 17 [lemonde.fr#1][euronews.com#1][straitstimes.com#1]. Students, unions, left-wing groups and Yellow Vest activists marched over living costs, housing, education and public services. Protesters also opposed a new law expanding legal protections for police who use firearms [lemonde.fr#1][globo.com#1].

Most marches were peaceful, but police used tear gas to disperse unauthorized gatherings in Lyon, and clashes and fires were reported in several cities. The Interior Ministry reported 144 arrests by 6 p.m. An AFP tally cited by French media counted at least 31 people seriously injured by security forces since the protests began; authorities have issued no official injury total [euronews.com#1][tass.com#1][lemonde.fr#1][rt-english.com#1].

Youth- and worker-led rallies also took place in Portugal and Spain [aljazeera.com#1][euronews.com#1]. French unions have called another public-sector strike and demonstrations for Dec. 1, demanding higher public-sector pay and renewed wage negotiations [aa.com.tr#1][watson.ch#1].
quote: In a number of countries, young people are going through the same thing, namely precarity. You have to choose between having a roof over your head, getting medical care, and being able to eat your fill.
quote_author: Manon Moret, general secretary of the Unef students’ union
talking_points: Paris turnout: Police counted 21,500 participants in the capital, while organizers estimated 45,000 [tass.com#1][euronews.com#1].

Police law: The Senate passed the law 205-110. It presumes officers acted lawfully when using firearms, though evidence can rebut that presumption. The left says it will challenge the measure before the Constitutional Council [globo.com#1][descifrado.com#1].
Housing pressure: In Portugal, average annual earnings in 2025 were 37% below the EU average, while house prices had more than doubled since 2017 [euronews.com#1][dawn.com#1].

Care-home protest: In Madrid, demonstrators demanded accountability and compensation for 7,291 care-home deaths during the first COVID-19 wave in 2020 and called for publicly run care homes [euronews.com#1].

perspectives.text: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez: After passage of the police firearms law, Nunez urged regional authorities to be “particularly vigilant regarding the groups most hostile to law enforcement” [lemonde.fr#1].
Gabriel Amard, France Unbowed lawmaker: He criticized the new law, arguing that it shifts the presumption in police shooting cases toward treating the shooting as lawful [globo.com#1].
French trade unions CFDT, CGT and Unsa: Public-sector unions want an increase in the salary base rate, but the government has ruled out raising it in 2027 [aa.com.tr#1].

title: Finnish officials suspect Ukraine struck Russian cargo ship in Gulf of Finland
summary:
The Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire after two drones struck it in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, then drifted into Finnish waters. Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen said Ukraine was likely responsible, though Kyiv had not commented [abc.net.au#1][bbc.co.uk#1]. The 16 crew members left the ship for a nearby Russian vessel, while Finnish authorities led the rescue operation as the fire continued to burn [abc.net.au#1][japantoday.com#1].

The ship was bound for Kaliningrad and has links to Oboronlogistika, a Russian logistics company that serves the Defence Ministry. Finland’s Border Guard said the ship’s cargo was unconfirmed and could include military material. The ship is under U.S. sanctions [abc.net.au#1][japantoday.com#1]. Finnish authorities also suspected that a Russian helicopter briefly entered Finnish airspace hours after the strike, possibly during rescue or surveillance operations [dw.com#1][afp.com#1].

Finland imposed temporary air and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland, informed its allies and began coordinating the response. Russian vessels could tow the damaged ship back [abc.net.au#1][bbc.co.uk#1][energyconnects.com#1]. Finland’s defence minister said the Border Guard would investigate the attack with other authorities [bbc.co.uk#1].
quote: The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor.
quote_author: Petteri Orpo, Prime Minister of Finland
talking_points: Drone barrage: Leningrad Region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said Russian air defences downed 80 drones over the region overnight, though the figure has not been independently verified [helsinkitimes.com#1][energyconnects.com#1].
Ust-Luga damage: Drone strikes also damaged Novatek’s oil-product terminal and petroleum-product infrastructure at Ust-Luga, Ukraine’s Security Service said [energyconnects.com#1].

Diesel exports: Baltic ports’ role in fuel trade grew after an October agreement allowed Russia to partially resume diesel exports; the first tanker carrying diesel left Primorsk that month [energyconnects.com#1].
Ship dimensions: The Russian-flagged Sparta II is 121 metres long and left St. Petersburg for Kaliningrad on Friday, according to shipping data cited by Reuters [japantoday.com#1][indiatoday.in#1].

perspectives.text: Alexei Besprozvannykh, Governor of Kaliningrad: He said the incident posed no threat to supplies reaching the Russian exclave [bbc.co.uk#1].

Kristen Michal, Prime Minister of Estonia: He said the attack showed the consequences of resisting Russian aggression had reached the Baltic Sea and that Estonia would continue supporting Ukraine [timeslive.co.za#1].

Aleksandr Drozdenko, Governor of Leningrad Region: He initially said the crew did not need evacuation and planned to resume the voyage after completing necessary work. Finnish authorities later reported that the crew had left the ship [afp.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

title: Iran strikes Bahrain as Hormuz tanker attacks deepen Gulf standoff
summary:
Bahrain said an Iranian attack caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, Nov. 21, causing material damage but no injuries. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had instead targeted U.S. positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases with missiles and drones, claiming it hit two Patriot air-defense radars. Bahrain reported intercepting several incoming attacks, and the U.S. military had not confirmed damage to its bases [firstpost.com#1][aljazeera.com#1][timesofisrael.com#1][straitstimes.com#1].

Projectiles also struck two tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center. Iran’s army said another vessel caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted area, while the U.S. military said it had cleared mines from the main routes. The strait carried about one-fifth of global oil before the war. Iran has sought to restrict shipping through it, while the United States has imposed a counter-blockade of Iranian ports [al-monitor.com#1][ndtv.com#1][timesofisrael.com#1].

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said a Qatari delegation held two hours of mediation talks in Tehran on Friday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran would not discuss reopening the strait until its demands—including an end to the war and U.S. blockade—were met. Iran’s electricity company said rolling power cuts would begin Sunday, Nov. 22, citing fuel supply conditions [firstpost.com#1][aljazeera.com#1][khaleejtimes.com#1].
quote: Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless.
quote_author: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi
talking_points: Tanker damage: The maritime agency said one tanker was hit in the stern and another in its engine room; no casualties were reported in either incident [timesofisrael.com#1][ndtv.com#1].
Oil movement: U.S. Central Command said last month it had helped Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels through Hormuz since the summer [al-monitor.com#1][firstpost.com#1].

title: Canada says military ties with U.S. continue as Ottawa diversifies
summary:
Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said he had seen no change in military cooperation with the United States despite a reported Pentagon directive limiting some contacts. He said Canadian officials had not seen the document [globalnews.ca#1][sootoday.com#1]. Republican Sen. Mike Rounds said the guidance mainly requires U.S. military officials to obtain permission to attend Canadian think-tank events or social functions and does not affect operations [independent.co.uk#1][lapresse.ca#1].

McGuinty cited ongoing cooperation between Canadian and U.S. forces, including ships operating together against drug trafficking in the Caribbean, integrated missile systems and fighter jets dispatched across North America when needed [cna.com.tw#1][firstpost.com#1]. He said Canada had decided 18 months ago to diversify its military relationships and described its relationship with the U.S. as strong [globalnews.ca#1].

Ottawa is also seeking to take greater responsibility for its own defence, including in the Arctic, and is developing a communications system to compete with Starlink, McGuinty said [cna.com.tw#1][firstpost.com#1]. Canada has formally joined NATO’s Innovation Fund, a venture-capital fund for advanced technologies, and is contributing more than $100 million to support investment in Canadian start-ups [lapresse.ca#1][sootoday.com#1].
quote: If something else evolves, we’ll deal with it.
quote_author: Defence Minister David McGuinty
talking_points: Domestic production: Defence Minister David McGuinty said Canada wants to buy less military hardware from the U.S. and build more at home across 10 core areas, turning first to partner countries for foreign purchases [breakingdefense.com#1].

Innovation funding: Canada became the fund’s 25th member; the NATO-backed fund invests in areas including artificial intelligence, quantum technology, biotechnology, space and communications [lapresse.ca#1].

Senate criticism: Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine called the directive’s tone “bad” and “unnecessary,” while Sen. Chris Coons warned against further straining relations between the allies [globalnews.ca#1][independent.co.uk#1].
U.S. assessment: Rounds said Canadian officials viewed the described restrictions as consistent with practices already in place for about a year and a half [sootoday.com#1][independent.co.uk#1].

perspectives.text: Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty: He acknowledged that U.S. President Donald Trump’s threats prompted some recent Canadian defence-policy changes [firstpost.com#1].

Republican Sen. Mike Rounds: Rounds said the described restrictions do not affect U.S. defence personnel currently in Canada or cooperation through NORAD, NATO or the Five Eyes alliance [breakingdefense.com#1][lapresse.ca#1].

Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine: Kaine said he expected Democrats taking control of Congress in January to change the tone of U.S. policy, while acknowledging the new Congress could not change all three branches of government [globalnews.ca#1].

title: B.C. premier merges mining into resource ministry, removes climate portfolio
summary:
British Columbia Premier Lorne Doerkson unveiled a smaller cabinet on Nov. 20, combining mining with energy and petroleum resources and removing climate change from the names of key ministries [thenarwhal.ca#1][lethbridgeherald.com#1]. The cabinet has 18 ministers, plus Doerkson and six ministers of state; the former New Democratic government had 23 ministers. Doerkson’s Conservative government also says it will repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA), which provides for joint project decisions with First Nations [thenarwhal.ca#1][thehub.ca#1].

The new cabinet includes rookie MLAs in major portfolios. Finance Minister Peter Milobar says the government will commission an independent review of provincial finances; the latest forecast cited by The Canadian Press put the deficit at nearly $14 billion [lethbridgeherald.com#1][thetyee.ca#1]. Doerkson said the legislature will not sit this fall, though his government is considering orders-in-council. The Narwhal reported that MLAs are unlikely to return before February. The first cabinet meeting is scheduled for next week [thenarwhal.ca#1][lethbridgeherald.com#1].
quote: I am committed to repealing DRIPA because it hasn’t worked
quote_author: Lorne Doerkson, British Columbia premier
talking_points: Health portfolio: Health Minister Ryan Peterson will oversee a ministry with about $40 billion in expenses; Doerkson said he selected him for his business background [lethbridgeherald.com#1][thetyee.ca#1].

Resource projects: B.C. has 41 major projects, including 16 in critical minerals and mining; the Conservatives have pledged fixed permitting timelines and a “one project, one review” approach [thenarwhal.ca#1].

LNG target: The party’s platform promises to double liquefied natural gas production by 2032 and triple it by 2035; LNG Canada in Kitimat is the province’s only operating export facility [thenarwhal.ca#1].
Campaign spending: The Conservatives’ plan proposed adding $1.4 billion in annual operating spending while reducing the deficit within three years [lethbridgeherald.com#1][thetyee.ca#1].

perspectives.text: Scott McInnis, minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation: McInnis said reconciliation concerns everyone in B.C. and pointed to the province’s 204 First Nations as communities with distinct needs and challenges [thenarwhal.ca#1].

The Hub editorial: The Hub argued the cabinet’s reduced size and Doerkson’s selection by fellow legislators offer a better basis for governing than appointments shaped by leadership-campaign obligations [thehub.ca#1].

title: Former federal minister Navdeep Bains wins Ontario Liberal leadership
summary:
Former federal industry minister Navdeep Bains won the Ontario Liberal leadership on Saturday, beating Toronto-area member of provincial parliament Lee Fairclough by 50.3% to 49.7% on the third ballot. Bains, who has no seat in the provincial legislature, said he intends to run for one but did not say where or when. He ruled out asking a sitting Liberal MPP to resign for him [theglobeandmail.com#1][cbc.ca#1][sootoday.com#1].

Bains takes charge of a party with 14 seats, behind the governing Progressive Conservatives’ 79 and the New Democrats’ 27. The Liberals have lost three straight provincial elections since Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s party first took office in 2018, and the next election may not come until 2030. Bains campaigned on jobs, economic growth and affordability, while his critics have pointed to his ties to former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau [sootoday.com#2][torontosun.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1][cbc.ca#1].
quote: This may be the end of a leadership race, ladies and gentleman, but this is just the beginning of our campaign to replace Doug Ford and the Conservative Party of Ontario
quote_author: Navdeep Bains, Ontario Liberal leader
talking_points: Member turnout: Of about 55,000 eligible members, 20,510 cast ballots; the party reported turnout of roughly 37%, up from about 22% in its 2023 leadership vote [sootoday.com#2][theglobeandmail.com#1].

Ballot rounds: Bains led with 44.1% on the first ballot. Dylan Marando was eliminated in that round, followed by Stephanie Bowman in the second, when she received 15.7% [sootoday.com#2][nationalobserver.com#1].

Party outlook: A Liaison Strategies poll during the race found that all four candidates were little known to Ontario voters. A recent Abacus Data survey put the Liberals at 33%, behind the PCs at 39% and ahead of the NDP at 18% [nationalobserver.com#1][thestar.com#1].

perspectives.text: Navdeep Bains, Ontario Liberal leader: Bains said he wants to build a grassroots movement and raise more money than the party has ever raised to challenge Ford’s Conservatives [thestar.com#1].

Doug Ford, Ontario premier: Ford said families want parties to work collaboratively, put the province over party and focus on standing up to tariffs, protecting workers and making life more affordable [cbc.ca#1].

Erin Morrison, NDP strategist: Morrison argued Bains had not set out sufficiently concrete policies and said his former Rogers role contrasted with the NDP’s focus on affordability [theglobeandmail.com#1].

Lee Fairclough and Stephanie Bowman, Liberal leadership candidates and MPPs: Both candidates argued during the race that the party needed a leader already sitting in the legislature to challenge Ford directly [theglobeandmail.com#1].

title: Montreal police make first arrests in force misconduct probe
summary:
The first criminal arrests in a Montreal police misconduct investigation have prompted civil-rights advocates to call for accountability and wider scrutiny. One said the case could set a precedent for holding officers responsible [cbc.ca#1][montrealgazette.com#1]. Allegations involving a second station, downtown Station 21, include mistreatment of unhoused people and a claim that an officer urinated on someone while on duty [globalnews.ca#1][montrealgazette.com#1].

Quebec prosecutors charged former Montreal police officers Vincent Routhier and Zachary Belzil with assault and breach of trust; Belzil also faces a criminal-harassment charge. Both were released on promises to appear, and no court date had been set [cbc.ca#1][montrealgazette.com#1][ledevoir.com#1]. The force’s union is challenging the administrative dismissals of seven officers, and Chief Fady Dagher has said they could be reinstated if those challenges succeed [montrealgazette.com#1]. Related criminal investigations continue under the supervision of an independent observer appointed by Quebec’s public security ministry [thestar.com#1][montrealgazette.com#1].
quote: It validates everything we had hoped would take place
quote_author: Fo Niemi, executive director of the Center for Research-Action on Race Relations
talking_points: Other allegations: A Station 39 officer was accused of deleting evidence from a domestic-violence victim’s phone after recognizing the alleged abuser [thestar.com#1][montrealgazette.com#1].
Street checks: The Red Coalition says street checks enable racist and discriminatory policing and is calling on Montreal’s police service to end the practice [cbc.ca#1].
Dismissal process: Montreal police revoked the seven officers’ security clearances, allowing the force to dismiss them before criminal or disciplinary proceedings concluded [montrealgazette.com#1].

perspectives.text: Red Coalition: Founder and executive director Joel DeBellefeuille questioned why allegations were believed when raised within the police force but not when raised by the public. He said advocacy groups and residents had spoken out for decades without seeing action [thestar.com#1].

title: Toronto police arrest Canada’s ninth-most-wanted suspect in Scarborough murder
summary:
Toronto police arrested Devondre Hall, a 25-year-old Toronto man, on Friday, Nov. 20, and charged him with first-degree murder in the death of Marcus Charles, whose body was found in a burned vehicle in Scarborough in September [thestar.com#1][cbc.ca#1][torontotoday.ca#1]. Hall ranked ninth on the Be On The Lookout (BOLO) Program’s list of Canada’s 25 most wanted fugitives, released the day before his arrest [thestar.com#1][torontosun.com#1].

Police also arrested 26-year-old Shyanne Miller and charged her with being an accessory after the fact to murder [cbc.ca#1][thestar.com#1]. Two other people had already been arrested in the case: Rushon Powell, charged with first-degree murder, and Shakurwa Jeffrey, charged with being an accessory after the fact [thestar.com#1][cbc.ca#1]. Police have not said whether the killing is connected to a second fatal shooting in which a body was found in a burned vehicle in Etobicoke the same night. The investigation continues [torontotoday.ca#1][thestar.com#1][globalnews.ca#1].
talking_points: Scene details: Charles, 32, was found Sept. 21 near Reesor Road and Steeles Avenue East; investigators said he had been shot before the vehicle was burned [thestar.com#1][torontotoday.ca#1].

Separate killing: A second man, 30-year-old Mohamud Kheyre, was found shot dead in a burned vehicle near Royal York Road and Edenbridge Drive in Etobicoke at about 1 a.m. on Sept. 22 [torontotoday.ca#1][thestar.com#1].
Police appeal: Investigators are asking anyone with information about Charles’s death to contact Toronto police [globalnews.ca#1][torontotoday.ca#1].

title: European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission
summary:
BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet [apnews.com#1][eos.org#1][mainichi.jp#1]. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027 [space.com#1][eos.org#1].

The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind [eos.org#1][apnews.com#1].

Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away [apnews.com#1]. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029 [eos.org#1].
quote: What makes this mission really unique is that for the first time in space exploration, we are bringing two spacecraft to the vicinity of the planet, and we are going to put them in orbit around this mysterious body.
quote_author: Santa Martinez, European Space Agency mission manager for BepiColombo
talking_points: Orbital paths: Mio is headed for a highly elliptical polar orbit, while the European orbiter will use a less elliptical polar orbit [space.com#1].
Long route: The spacecraft made one Earth, two Venus and six Mercury flybys to shed speed; the looping trajectory covered more than 10 billion kilometers [apnews.com#1][space.com#1].
Energy challenge: Reaching Mercury is harder than reaching Pluto because a spacecraft must shed enough momentum to match Mercury’s path around the Sun [eos.org#1].
Mission cost: The joint mission is valued at about $2 billion, or 1.7 billion euros [apnews.com#1][eos.org#1].

technical_details: Gravity and radio measurements: The European orbiter’s altimeter will map surface elevation, while its accelerometer, gravitometer and radio-science experiment will help map Mercury’s gravity and determine the size of its core [eos.org#1].

Thermal management: The spacecraft use metallic-coated insulating films and multilayer insulation to manage temperature extremes; plans also call for one orbiter to spin 15 times per minute to reduce overheating [orf.at#1][tagesspiegel.de#1].
scientific_significance: Polar scans will search for water ice, while comparisons with MESSENGER observations may reveal changes on Mercury since that mission visited about a decade earlier [earthsky.org#1].

title: Ebola death toll in Congo exceeds 5,700 as response lags
summary:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 19, making it the country’s largest and deadliest. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria [time.com#1][elpais.com#1]. The Bundibugyo strain is driving the outbreak, and no approved vaccine or targeted treatment is available for it. Health workers say early cases can be difficult to identify because initial symptoms resemble those of other illnesses [time.com#1][theguardian.com#1].

Late detection, population movement and mistrust of response teams have hindered containment, while attacks on health workers and burial teams have further complicated the response [time.com#1][elpais.com#1]. On Nov. 17, health workers in Butembo, North Kivu, escalated a month-long strike over unpaid wages and bonuses, halting even minimum service at treatment centers [liberation.fr#1].
quote: Coming early, before there are complications, gives patients more chances of survival
quote_author: Vivuya Kavira Mwenga, nurse at the Doctors Without Borders Ebola treatment center in Beni
talking_points: Treatment outcomes: Six Ebola treatment centers supported by ALIMA have received 1,243 patients, nearly 70% of whom recovered, according to Le Potentiel [lepotentiel.cd#1].
Children at risk: Children accounted for 28% of confirmed cases but 35% of deaths; by Nov. 4, 1,737 of the 2,959 people under 18 with confirmed infections had died [elpais.com#1].

Cases reach Europe: France confirmed a case in June in a doctor returning from a humanitarian mission in Congo; a British doctor who tested positive in Congo in November was flown to London for treatment and recovered [time.com#1].

Funding shortfall: International Rescue Committee response director Katie Thomas-Canfield said cuts in U.S., U.K. and German aid weakened surveillance and community relationships before the outbreak grew [time.com#1].

perspectives.text: Doctors Without Borders (MSF): International president Dr. Javid Abdelmoneim said resources committed to the response were not effectively reaching patients, frontline staff and communities. He called the situation after six months unacceptable [elpais.com#1].
Julien Harneis, UN special coordinator for Ebola: Responding to MSF’s criticism, Harneis said teams could operate 80% of the time despite the area’s immense size [elpais.com#1].
Health workers in Butembo: They said negotiations were at an impasse after the provincial health coordinator failed to attend a meeting they had requested [liberation.fr#1].

timeline.content: The outbreak is estimated to have begun in mid-to-late February [time.com#1]
WHO detected the outbreak and declared it an emergency in mid-May [time.com#1]
The number of affected health zones increased from 60 to at least 68 after Sept. 1 [time.com#1]
Butembo health workers halted minimum service as they escalated their strike [liberation.fr#1]
Confirmed cases passed 11,700 and deaths exceeded 5,700 [time.com#1]

did_you_know: The current outbreak crossed 10,000 confirmed cases in 163 days, 51 days faster than the 2014-16 West African epidemic [time.com#1].

primary_image.caption: Vivuya Kavira Mwenga, 26, is a nurse at the Ebola treatment center (CTE) of Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Beni, in the province of North Kivu. She is one of the health professionals battling the current epidemic of this infectious disease, declared in mid-May in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The epidemic has already infected over 11,000 people and killed more than 5,400, according to the most recent data. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain and for which there is no treatment or approved vaccines, is already the second most serious one in history and the one spreading the fastest. The center's rooms are practically full. When patients come in, the team isolates them, closely monitors their state, and treats the symptoms. “We still cannot cure the Ebola caused by the virus Bundibugyo, but we can treat the symptoms," explains Mwenga. “Coming early, before there are complications, gives patients more chances of survival," adds the nurse. “When someone gets out of here alive, it's a tremendous source of joy," she says. “It's what we want for each and every one of our patients."

secondary_image.caption: Alice Alyerunga, 43, is a nursing supervisor from Bunia. She works at the CTE in Mongbwalu. "It's the most stressful intervention I've ever been involved in. It was catastrophic at first. For three weeks we didn't have any survivors. Around 100 people died. Every night, my heart bled for our patients. When we had our first survivor, it was a moment of immense joy," she recalls. "As frontline health workers, we are highly exposed, even wearing personal protective equipment. This makes working here scary, but we are motivated by our mission to save lives and break chains of transmission." "My family and daughter encouraged me to go help patients. They gave me their blessing. My friends are afraid for me, but I tell them that I am taking all the necessary measures to protect myself," she says.

title: Court halts Army plan to detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa
summary:
A federal court temporarily halted the U.S. Army’s plan to detonate 68 drums of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown after environmental groups challenged an emergency permit and raised concerns about lead dust spreading across Iowa and western Illinois [krdo.com#2][theconversation.com#1][cbsnews.com#1]. The Army had rescheduled the blasts for Monday, Nov. 23, after objections from the public and elected officials; the court’s pause leaves it unclear whether they can proceed that day [krdo.com#1][krdo.com#2].

The Army says the material became more sensitive to shock and friction after liquid evaporated during prolonged storage, making transport hazardous and controlled detonation the safest immediate option. The plan calls for wetting the soil and using sand barriers to limit airborne particles, but the amount of lead likely to escape remains uncertain [aljazeera.com#1][nbcchicago.com#1]. University of Iowa researchers and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency planned to sample air and surfaces. The EPA was expected to respond to the lawsuit by Nov. 22, while the judge set no date for further action [theconversation.com#1][krdo.com#2].
quote: The unprecedented aspect of it is that normally in the world of air pollution, we have some estimation of what’s called the emission factor, the emission strength. We know how many pounds per second will be distributed out into the air from a smokestack.
quote_author: Patrick O’Shaughnessy, University of Iowa professor of occupational and environmental health
talking_points: Alternative disposal: The Army hired Georgia-based MuniRem Environmental to chemically neutralize the explosives, then canceled the contract. The company’s chief executive said the Army offered no explanation beyond citing its safety assessment [nytimes.com#2][krdo.com#1].

Farm concerns: Some dairy farmers worried that cattle could ingest lead that settled on pasture grass. Most crops had already been harvested, reducing the potential for lead to settle on them [theconversation.com#1].

Exposure testing: University of Iowa researchers planned to collect airborne dust as the plume passed and use gauzelike pads to sample settled material, with laboratory results expected about a week after detonation [theconversation.com#1].
State response: Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds activated the state Emergency Operations Center, while Cedar Rapids prepared to monitor drinking water drawn from the Mississippi River [krdo.com#1].

perspectives.text: U.S. Army: Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said the Army moved the operation to Monday as the latest possible moment before a forecast temperature drop that could further destabilize the material [krdo.com#1].

Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club’s Iowa chapter: The groups asked a federal appeals court to overturn the emergency permit, arguing the public lacked meaningful advance notice, safeguards were inadequate and safer disposal options had not been sufficiently considered [aljazeera.com#1].

Illinois Department of Public Health: Director Sameer Vohra advised potentially affected Illinois residents to remain indoors with windows closed for 24 to 48 hours and wash hands and outdoor surfaces to reduce exposure [nbcchicago.com#1].

technical_details: Stockpile composition: The 68 barrels held about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, containing roughly 6,900 pounds of lead by chemical mass [aljazeera.com#1].
Blast effects: The Army warned that noise and ground vibrations from the detonation could cause localized window damage [krdo.com#2].

Forecast conditions: For the rescheduled Nov. 23 date, the preliminary forecast called for slower winds toward the south-southeast, potentially affecting a smaller area but bringing higher lead concentrations to those downwind [theconversation.com#1].
scientific_significance: Lead persistence: Lead cannot be destroyed by heat; experts said the blast could convert or disperse it into fine particles and compounds that settle into soil and on outdoor surfaces [aljazeera.com#1].
Model estimates: The Army's models predicted elevated airborne lead levels, but below the threshold at which the EPA would require protective actions [aljazeera.com#1].
Health vulnerability: Lead exposure can harm the brain and nervous system, and experts highlighted particular risks for young children and developing fetuses [theconversation.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: What would happen if the court allows the operation to proceed?
suggested_qna.answer: Fort Madison officials said they had been told the detonation could happen Monday or Tuesday. If it did not take place that week, another date would need to be arranged with additional planning [krdo.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: What cleanup steps are recommended after the plume passes?
suggested_qna.answer: The Army recommended hosing down windowsills, cars and other horizontal surfaces where dust could collect, and washing outdoor toys and play areas. Washing moves lead from surfaces into soil rather than eliminating it [theconversation.com#1].

historical_background: The material had been in storage for more than 20 years before its deterioration was discovered [krdo.com#1][nbcchicago.com#1]. The emergency permit authorized detonation through Feb. 11, 2027, and required the Army to track potential air and dust dispersion and notify the public five days in advance [nbcchicago.com#1][krdo.com#1].

title: Trump threatens tax on overseas AI data centers as chip curbs tighten
summary:
President Donald Trump threatened to impose a “tremendous tax” on U.S. companies that build artificial intelligence data centers abroad, saying he wants computing capacity concentrated in the United States to keep pace with China. He offered no details on how the tax would work and said he had not yet told his advisers about the proposal [etoday.co.kr#1]. Separately, the Commerce Department issued new licensing requirements targeting Chinese access to advanced U.S. chips, including remote access through overseas servers [fortune.com#1][cnn.com#1].

U.S.-based infrastructure also delivers Chinese AI models to global customers. Some overseas data centers help companies comply with local data-storage rules and reduce transmission delays [fortune.com#1][etoday.co.kr#1]. Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are due to meet at the G20 summit in December; the countries’ trade truce is set to expire Jan. 10, 2027 [cnn.com#1].
quote: China can hit back, and they can hit back hard.
quote_author: Han Lin, China country director for The Asia Group
talking_points: U.S. infrastructure concentration: Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon design nearly all deployed data-center AI chips, while Amazon, Microsoft and Google together control more than half of cloud services [fortune.com#1].
China’s alternatives: Huawei is developing an Atlas 950 SuperPoD designed to link as many as 8,192 Ascend chips; it demonstrated a 1,024-chip network in July [hani.co.kr#1].

Local opposition: U.S. communities have raised concerns about data centers’ electricity demand, utility bills and water use. A bill passed by the Senate would require large facilities to cover their own power costs; it still needs House approval [etoday.co.kr#1].
Industrial policy: China’s 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan prioritizes technological self-reliance, advanced manufacturing and wider AI adoption [firstpost.com#1].

perspectives.text: President Donald Trump: He argued that U.S. companies should build data centers at home rather than overseas and suggested firms could negotiate with local communities over electricity costs, tax breaks and other benefits [etoday.co.kr#1].

Kyle Chan, Brookings Institution: Chan said Chinese firms can draw on shared industrial expertise and supply networks, but government priorities for expanding capacity may conflict with companies’ commercial returns [firstpost.com#1].
